request: how can a polynomial pretend to be cos x?

beats.narration: Here is cos x, rising and falling forever.
beats.code:
stage.title("Pretending to be cos x")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(-4, 4), y_range=(-2, 2))
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, np.cos, color=BLUE, label=r"\cos x")

beats.intent: Polynomials 1, 1 - x²/2, 1 - x²/2 + x⁴/24 hugging the curve near 0
beats.narration: Match its value at zero, then its curvature, then more: each polynomial hugs the curve a little further out.

beats.intent: The polynomial beside cos x ≈ 1 - x²/2 + x⁴/24
beats.narration: Three terms already match cos x well out past one.

beats.intent: A check at x = 1: 0.5417 against cos 1 = 0.5403
beats.narration: At x equals one, the polynomial gives 0.5417; the true value is 0.5403.

request: why is the area of a circle pi r squared?

beats.intent: A circle cut into 12 coloured slices
beats.narration: Cut a circle into twelve slices, like a pizza.

beats.intent: The slices laid alternately up and down into a near-rectangle
beats.narration: Lay them out, alternately tip up and tip down. They make a bumpy rectangle.

beats.intent: The near-rectangle with height r and width πr labelled
beats.narration: Its height is the radius r. Its width is half the circumference: pi r.
beats.code:
stage.label(rect, r"\pi r", direction=DOWN, color=YELLOW)
stage.label(rect, "r", direction=RIGHT, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: The rectangle beside area = πr · r = πr²
beats.narration: More slices make it a true rectangle, so the area is pi r times r: pi r squared.

request: show me the sieve of Eratosthenes up to 50

beats.intent: The numbers 2 to 50 set out in a grid
beats.narration: Write the numbers up to fifty. Two is the first prime.
beats.code:
stage.title("The sieve of Eratosthenes")
grid = sieve_primes(stage, n=50)

beats.intent: The sieved grid beside π(50) = 15, the count of primes up to 50
beats.narration: Crossing out the multiples of two, three, five and seven leaves fifteen primes.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\pi(50) = 15")
stage.caption("Multiples of 2, 3, 5 and 7 crossed out")

beats.intent: Bars of how many primes lie in each block of 10 up to 50
beats.narration: They thin out: four in the first ten, then four, two, two, three.

request: what does the derivative of x squared mean at x = 1?

beats.intent: The parabola y = x² on axes with the point (1, 1) marked
beats.narration: Take the parabola y equals x squared, and the point one, one.
beats.code:
stage.title("The slope at x = 1")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(-1, 3), y_range=(-1, 6))
f = lambda x: x ** 2
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, f)
p = mark_point(stage, ax, (1, 1), color=RED, label="(1, 1)")

beats.intent: A secant from x = 1 to x = 3 shrinking into the tangent
beats.narration: Draw a line through it and a second point. Slide the second point in: the line becomes the tangent.

beats.intent: The tangent beside the limit of (1 + h)² - 1 over h equals 2
beats.narration: The secant's slope is two plus h. As h shrinks, it heads to two.

beats.intent: The slope 2 read as a rise of 2 for each 1 across on the tangent
beats.narration: So at x equals one, the curve climbs two for every one step across.
beats.code:
run = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(1, 1), ax.c2p(2, 1), color=GREEN)
rise = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(2, 1), ax.c2p(2, 3), color=YELLOW)
stage.label(rise, "2", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)
stage.caption("f'(1) = 2")
